stories.summary: Alibaba has launched Qwen4-Max, the flagship of its Qwen AI family, and for the first time for this line it is keeping the model weights closed, so users cannot download or modify it. The 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model handles text, images and video and accepts prompts up to one million tokens. Alibaba says its coding scores beat Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, but published charts show it trailing Claude Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (48.5 against 59.6). API pricing is $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens, and Alibaba says average task cost fell from $4.43 to $1.67 on an internal test. The launch comes amid a flurry of Chinese model releases and scrutiny of earlier Qwen models over sandbox behaviour. Smaller Qwen4 models are promised open weights, with no date given.
key_points: Alibaba launched Qwen4-Max, its flagship AI model, with closed weights for the first time in the Qwen line.
The model is a 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts system handling text, images and video, with prompts up to one million tokens.
Alibaba's own coding benchmarks put it ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 and Kimi K3.1 Pro, but it trails on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (48.5 vs 59.6 for Claude Opus 5.5).
API pricing is $1.50 per million input and $4.50 per million output tokens.
Alibaba says a task cost on its internal test fell from $4.43 to $1.67 versus Qwen3.8-Max.
Smaller Qwen4 models are promised open weights, with no date given.
stories.market_take: Could support sentiment around Chinese AI and chip names, and T-Head's Hong Kong IPO is a watch point for Alibaba.

stories.headline: Estonia to close border with Russia after second alleged sabotage attempt
stories.claim: Estonia plans to close all border crossings with Russia from 1 December after a failed arson attack on a drone maker.
stories.summary: Estonia plans to close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December, after a failed arson attack on Threod Systems, a drone maker near Tallinn. Estonian authorities say the attack, in the early hours of 14 November, was ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence. Eight Latvian residents have been detained, and prosecutors want five remanded in custody. Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna says the closure will limit Russia's ability to run hostile operations and prevent sanctions evasion. The move follows an August arson attack on Milrem Robotics, which Estonia blamed on Russian intelligence in September. The government is expected to finalise the measures in the coming days.
key_points: Estonia will close all border crossings with Russia from 1 December, according to Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna.
The attempted arson hit Threod Systems, which makes reconnaissance and attack drones, at about 3am on 14 November.
Estonia's security service KAPO says the suspects tried to cause an explosion and fire at the Viimsi site.
Eight Latvian residents have been detained, and five may be held in custody.
This is the second alleged sabotage on an Estonian defence firm, after the Milrem Robotics attack in August.
The government is expected to finalise the border closure in the coming days.
stories.market_take: Limited direct market effect; European defence stocks may see sentiment support from the sabotage news.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin set for first trilateral nuclear talks at APEC in Shenzhen
stories.claim: Trump, Xi and Putin are set to hold the first trilateral meeting on nuclear arms control on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen, with no agreement expected.
stories.summary: The White House has confirmed that Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will meet on Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, which would be the first in-person meeting of the three leaders, though China has not formally confirmed it. Nuclear arms reduction is expected to be the main topic, with Iran possibly raised and Ukraine reportedly not on the agenda, but a senior US official said no agreement is expected. The meeting follows the expiry of the New START treaty in February, which left no major arms control limits between Washington and Moscow. Trump wants a new treaty that includes China, which has rejected joining trilateral nuclear talks, saying it is neither fair nor realistic at this stage. Trump arrived late on Wednesday for the two-day summit and holds a bilateral lunch with Xi before the trilateral, their fourth meeting since 2025. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the agenda and format had not yet been agreed. China's Foreign Ministry called the meeting of groundbreaking significance, and UN chief Antonio Guterres said the UN would support any denuclearisation effort. Trump is also on a four-day Asia trip including a Quad meeting and a US-ASEAN summit in Manila, and the Yalta comparison has drawn commentary.
key_points: The White House confirmed a Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting on Thursday in Shenzhen, though China has not formally confirmed it.
Nuclear arms reduction is expected to be the main topic, but a senior US official said no agreement is expected.
New START expired in February, leaving no major US-Russia arms control limits.
China has said it is neither fair nor realistic to join trilateral nuclear disarmament talks at this stage.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the agenda and format have not been agreed, and Trump is on a four-day Asia trip.
stories.market_take: Any trade or tech breakthrough, or a flare-up in tensions, could move Asian equities and the yuan.

stories.headline: PM Burnham says Brexit has not worked as UK prepares to sign EU food reset deal
stories.claim: PM Andy Burnham says Brexit 'has not worked' and will sign an EU food reset deal at a summit on Friday.
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Brexit "has not worked" and will sign a new agreement with the EU at a summit on Friday, telling the Lord Mayor's Banquet in the City of London that Britain has lost more than it gained. The package, covering food and farming, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme, is calculated to add 0.4% to UK GDP, about £17bn. Relations minister Hamish Falconer said the UK would get a "voice in the room" but no vote on EU food rules, with food-specific gains of about £5bn and lower paperwork and costs for exporters and eventually shoppers. An "exit clause" is under consideration so a future government could not easily reverse closer alignment, a feature the EU wants because of the cost of rebuilding border checks. A draft SPS text reportedly would make any party leaving pay for restoring controls, a provision EU diplomats call the "Farage clause", which UK sources dispute as routine and mutual. The Conservatives and Reform have both pledged to undo the reset if elected. The National Farmers' Union welcomed fewer checks but wants to see carve-outs, while Boris Johnson said Britain would "absolutely" vote for Brexit again and Nigel Farage called the stance a "total betrayal".
key_points: Andy Burnham says Brexit "has not worked" and will sign a new EU deal at a summit on Friday.
The package is calculated to add 0.4% to UK GDP, about £17bn, across food, emissions trading and youth mobility.
Falconer says the UK gets a "voice in the room" but no vote on EU food rules, with food gains of about £5bn.
An exit clause is under consideration; a draft SPS text reportedly would make a leaving party pay for restoring border controls, dubbed the "Farage clause".
The Conservatives and Reform have pledged to undo the reset if elected.
The NFU welcomed fewer checks but is waiting to see carve-outs and transitional arrangements.
stories.market_take: A closer EU deal could support UK exporters and sterling sentiment, though details are still to be negotiated.

stories.headline: AO3 fan fiction site back online after two-week outage
stories.claim: Fan fiction site AO3 is back online after a security-related outage of about two weeks, with some features still disabled.
stories.summary: The Archive of Our Own (AO3), the volunteer-run fan fiction site with nearly 19 million works and about 12 million users, is mostly back online after a security incident took it offline in late October. It returned earlier than the four-week restoration it had promised, on Sunday, with some features such as importing external works and icons still disabled. Works can only be downloaded as HTML for now. The nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works says no works, bookmarks or kudos were deleted and it has no reason to believe the user database was compromised, though it cannot rule this out. It has not disclosed what happened, is working with a security firm, and has advised users to change passwords, particularly where they reuse them. Traffic surges caused loading delays, which the site said were deliberate. Draft deletion resumes on 29 November, when drafts older than 30 days will be removed.
key_points: AO3 returned on Sunday, earlier than the four weeks originally promised.
Icons and external work importing remain disabled, and works can only be downloaded as HTML.
The nonprofit says no works, bookmarks or kudos were deleted.
AO3 says it has no reason to believe the user database was compromised but cannot rule it out.
Users are advised to change passwords, especially where reused elsewhere.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO over affair with suspected Chinese spy; Kress interim CEO
stories.claim: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on 12 November over disclosed affairs; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and the board is searching for a successor.
stories.summary: Nvidia's board has ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive, with chair Harvey Jones saying so on the company's third-quarter earnings call, even as the chipmaker beat Wall Street forecasts. Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member on 12 November after admitting extramarital affairs, one reportedly with Alice Huang, a Singapore-based executive whom US officials suspect was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security; Beijing calls the claims a smear. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim chief executive, and Harvey Jones became the company's first independent chair. Shares fell as much as 14% in early trading after the resignation and closed down just over 4%, with roughly $1 trillion of market value lost that month. The Financial Times reported Huang was discussing a return and a petition gathered more than 115,000 signatures, but the board has now rebuffed him. Nvidia may lack full insurance cover for executive conduct, raising lawsuit risk.
key_points: Nvidia's board chair Harvey Jones said on the earnings call that Huang will not be reinstated as CEO.
Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member on 12 November after admitting extramarital affairs, one reportedly with Alice Huang.
US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security; China calls the claims a smear.
Colette Kress, CFO since 2013, is interim CEO while Heidrick & Struggles runs a search covering internal and external candidates.
Shares fell as much as 14% early on the Friday after the resignation, closed down just over 4%, and about $1 trillion of value was lost that month.
Nvidia may lack full insurance cover for executive conduct, raising lawsuit risk.
signals: Reliable source: Financial Times (original report)
Company says it has not formally engaged any candidates
Single original report cited by other outlets

stories.headline: Behind the All-American Ralph Lauren Brand Is a French C.E.O.
stories.claim: Ralph Lauren's French chief executive Patrice Louvet has turned the American brand around since 2017, with shares up over 400%.
stories.summary: Ralph Lauren's share price has risen more than 400 percent since Patrice Louvet became chief executive in 2017, a striking turnaround for a company that was at a low point when he arrived. The French former Procter & Gamble executive, who spent nearly 30 years in consumer goods and once served in the French Navy, cut heavy discounting and pulled the brand out of lower-tier stores. Its preppy look is back with younger shoppers, and the company posted $8.1 billion in revenue last fiscal year, up 14 percent. It recently raised its sales and margin forecast for the current year ahead of the holiday season. The Lauren family still controls more than 80 percent of the shareholder vote, and founder Ralph Lauren, 87, remains chief creative officer and executive chairman.

Ralph Lauren's share price has risen more than 400 percent since he took the top job.
Last fiscal year revenue reached $8.1 billion, a 14 percent increase.

stories.headline: Too Many Chips in One Basket?
stories.claim: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned after revelations of two affairs, one reportedly with a suspected Chinese spy, and Nvidia's stock has tumbled.
stories.summary: Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, has resigned, weeks after he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials believe to be a Chinese spy. A second affair, this time with a subordinate, then came to light and he stepped down shortly afterwards. Nvidia's shares have fallen sharply since, wiping out hundreds of billions of dollars in market value. The column uses the episode to examine how much of the AI industry depends on one individual, and whether leaders who cannot easily be replaced leave their firms exposed. The piece is an opinion column, but the resignation and share fall are the key facts.

A second affair, with a subordinate, came to light shortly after and Huang resigned as chief executive.
Nvidia's stock has fallen sharply, losing hundreds of billions of dollars in value in the days since.
Analysts are assessing how the loss of a figure seen as central to the AI boom will play out.

stories.headline: Bessent says Nvidia needs a dramatic shakeup, outside CEO, and answers on China chip sales
stories.claim: Treasury Secretary Bessent called for a 'dramatic shakeup' at Nvidia, an outside CEO, and answers on China-linked chip sales.
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia and said the chipmaker should hire its next chief executive from outside the company. He demanded that the board and outside counsel answer within 10 days whether Nvidia knowingly ignored warning signs that shell companies, many based in Singapore, were routing advanced AI chips to China. Bessent made the remarks on Fox News and in a CNBC interview, where he questioned whether Nvidia knew its customers were pass-through shell companies and said anyone responsible should be held accountable. He stopped short of saying Jensen Huang knew of the practices, criticised general counsel Timothy Teter for contacting Commerce about the detention of Megaspeed's Alice Wong in Singapore, and said existing export rules should be enforced rather than tightened. He also said Treasury, War, State and USTR backed adding Megaspeed to the Entity List, but that Commerce's BIS reportedly stalled the move over China trade concerns. The intervention is unusual for a cabinet-level official targeting a single company and raises pressure on Nvidia ahead of its results on 17 November.
key_points: Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia and said the next chief executive should come from outside the company.
He demanded that the board and outside counsel answer within 10 days whether Nvidia knowingly pursued China-linked shell company sales.

Bessent opposed new export-control legislation, arguing existing rules should be enforced.
stories.market_take: Political pressure over export compliance could weigh on Nvidia shares and sentiment around its AI chip sales.

stories.headline: Judge blocks Trump administration from closing DC East Potomac golf course for now
stories.claim: A federal judge temporarily blocked the Trump administration from closing East Potomac Park's golf course in Washington for a planned 15-month redevelopment.
stories.summary: US District Judge Ana Reyes issued a temporary restraining order just before a closure of East Potomac Park's golf course was due to begin on Sunday 15 November, a 15-month renovation that would have created a championship course designed by Tom Fazio. In a 30-page decision issued Saturday, Reyes called the government's justifications pretextual and found it had broken at least two federal laws to meet an arbitrary deadline. The order runs through 28 November and requires the park to stay open to the public, although the administration does not have to run golf operations there. Trump said his administration will immediately appeal on an expedited basis, calling the decision highly destructive and political, while the Justice Department said the ruling does not stop planning for the course. The case was brought by the DC Preservation League and others, including two local golfers who argue the redevelopment would make the course unaffordable and change its character. Earlier, the National Park Service cut hundreds of trees in October with only 15 hours' notice to the court, and Reyes has opened an inquiry, with a special master, into whether Justice Department lawyers misled the court. The ruling is one of several court setbacks for Trump's Washington projects, which also include a memorial arch, a White House ballroom and the Kennedy Center.
key_points: Judge Ana Reyes issued a temporary restraining order blocking the closure just before it was due to start on Sunday 15 November.
The 30-page decision called the government's justifications pretextual and found at least two federal laws were broken.
The order runs through 28 November, and the park must stay open to the public.
Trump says the administration will appeal on an expedited basis; the Justice Department says planning can continue.
Reyes has opened an inquiry into whether Justice Department lawyers misled the court, including over late notice of tree felling.

stories.headline: Bangladesh garment factories shut as workers strike over minimum wage
stories.claim: Garment factories in Bangladesh's Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur hubs have shut as workers strike for a 30,000-taka minimum wage.
stories.summary: Owners in Bangladesh's main garment hubs are moving toward indefinite closures as workers strike over the minimum wage. Nearly 150 factories in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur shut over the weekend, and employer groups say plants that cannot operate will stay closed indefinitely from Monday under labour law. Earlier reports put the number of affected plants far higher, with owners in Ashulia, Jamgora and Hemayetpur weighing the closure of 210 factories ahead of an emergency meeting, and nine factories in Ashulia and Savar having already shut, affecting about 200,000 workers. Workers are demanding a minimum wage of 30,000 to 32,000 taka a month, up from 12,500 taka, while employers say even 30,000 taka is unaffordable amid high inflation, an energy crisis and new US tariffs. Protests have brought clashes, tear gas, dozens of arrests and more than 500 temporary closures, and a worker reportedly died after being beaten. The sector earns nearly $40bn a year and employs about four million people, supplying H&M, Primark and Zara. A government wage board is due to finish recommendations by the end of November, with any new pay due from 1 December.
key_points: Nearly 150 garment factories in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur closed over the weekend, and employer groups say they will stay shut indefinitely from Monday under labour law.
Workers want a minimum wage of 30,000 taka a month, up from 12,500 taka; some earlier reports cited 32,000 taka.
A government wage board is due to report by the end of November, with any new pay expected from 1 December.

stories.headline: Tesla opens invite-only Cybercab sales at $29,990 plus $299 monthly subscription
stories.claim: Tesla has begun inviting select customers to buy the Cybercab for $29,990 plus a mandatory $299-a-month subscription, with December delivery in Texas and Florida.
stories.summary: Tesla has begun inviting select customers to buy its Cybercab robotaxi for personal use at $29,990 before tax, with a mandatory $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription and a $1,000 non-refundable deposit. Estimated delivery is December 2026, and operation is limited to Tesla's Robotaxi zones in Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, San Antonio, Miami, Orlando and Tampa. Orders were announced via Tesla's Robotaxi account on X, and there is no public order page or stated method for choosing invitees. Elon Musk has conceded the monthly fee is too high and suggested it should be closer to $115, and said the car will be available nationwide once regulatory approval arrives. Electrek calculates the subscription adds about $47,600 over five years. The offer comes as an NHTSA inquiry into whether a car without a brake pedal meets federal safety standards remains open. YouTuber Marques Brownlee, who had bet Tesla would not deliver a Cybercab under $30,000 before 2027, reportedly received an invite but says the bet is not yet won because there are no deliveries.

A $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription is required to operate the car, and Electrek estimates about $47,600 over five years.

stories.market_take: Tesla's Cybercab pricing and subscription model could shape sentiment on its robotaxi revenue plans, though the impact is limited to a small invitation-only launch.

stories.headline: Oil prices rise on fresh Middle East attacks despite IEA report of oil supply surplus
stories.claim: Oil prices rose on Monday as fresh Middle East attacks and threats to Strait of Hormuz shipments revived supply worries.
stories.summary: Oil prices rose on Monday as fresh attacks across the Middle East and threats to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz revived supply concerns. The gain came despite forecasts of a global oil supply surplus that had been weighing on the market. The Strait of Hormuz carries a large share of the world's seaborne oil, so any disruption there tends to move prices quickly. The reports give no figures for the size of the move or the latest Brent or WTI price levels. Traders may reverse the gain if the attacks prove contained, and a lasting disruption could push up fuel costs for consumers in the UK, US and Europe.

stories.claim: Iran's IRGC says a supertanker sank after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, with no independent confirmation yet.

With Donald Trump reportedly planning to raise the conflict at a trilateral meeting with China and Russia this week, the escalation adds pressure on oil prices and shipping insurance.

stories.summary: A House of Lords committee has recommended that UK workers be given a new right to paid time off to train and volunteer for national emergencies, which it calls civic resilience leave. The 12-strong national resilience committee, reporting on Monday, says Britain remains underprepared for threats including war, power cuts, cyber-attacks and natural disasters. It also urges councils to register volunteers and list emergency shelters, and wants booklets sent to every household, as in Sweden and Denmark, plus a multilingual preparedness app. The report welcomes the government's recent campaign to stock tinned food and bottled water, but says the public lacks the full picture on threats from Russia, China and Iran. The Cabinet Office says it will carefully review the report and points to existing work on the war book and a national resilience exercise next year.
key_points: The committee proposes a new 'civic resilience leave' right to paid time off for approved training and emergency volunteering.
It recommends councils compile registers of skilled volunteers and lists of emergency shelters.
Peers want household booklets and a multilingual public preparedness app with automatic location sharing.
The report calls the government's stockpiling campaign a welcome step but says Britain is still underprepared.
The Cabinet Office says it will carefully review the report and cites a national resilience exercise scheduled for next year.

stories.headline: French presidential election: Meet the contenders you didn’t see coming
stories.claim: A growing field of would-be challengers, including ECB chief Christine Lagarde and judoka Teddy Riner, is emerging ahead of France's presidential election.
stories.summary: The French presidential race is widening beyond its established figures, with moderates struggling and far-left Jean-Luc Mélenchon surging in the polls. ECB President Christine Lagarde, who will leave her post on 7 February, has said she can no longer stay neutral and is widely seen as a possible candidate, polling on a par with Edouard Philippe in a POLITICO survey. Olympic judoka Teddy Riner, 37, has announced a run despite having no political experience, polling at 2 percent in an early survey. Former EU commissioner Thierry Breton and former economy minister Bruno Le Maire are also weighing bids. The field matters because it could shape whether the contest becomes a far-right versus far-left showdown.

stories.headline: A major breakthrough has claimed to set a world record for encoding data onto a quantum computer — and, crucially, reading it back again
stories.claim: Moth Quantum says its Tessa method stored 1,568 values on IBM's 120-qubit processor and read them back, claiming a record.
stories.summary: Moth Quantum says its Tessa technique has set a quantum computing record by loading 1,568 numerical values onto IBM's 120-qubit Phoenix processor and retrieving them. The earlier comparable work recovered 128 values using 12 trapped-ion qubits. Recovery was imperfect, however: the best colour image reached a correlation of 0.69 with its source, against 0.95 to 0.96 for simpler images. Tests on biological sequences were far less reliable, with some protein sequences recovered at between 22 and 92 percent accuracy. The results come from the company's own study, which did not use error correction or error mitigation, so the claim has yet to be independently verified.

stories.headline: WHO says antimicrobial resistance efforts improve globally but remain off track for 2030 goals
stories.claim: WHO survey finds 173 of 183 countries have antimicrobial resistance plans, but only 42 have them funded and implemented.
stories.summary: Only 42 of 183 countries say their national plans to fight antimicrobial resistance are both funded and implemented, despite 173 now having a plan, the World Health Organization has said. The gap leaves the world off track for its 2030 targets. The annual survey, run with UN Environment, the animal health body and the FAO, shows progress on paper but weak delivery. One in six lab-confirmed bacterial infections now resists antibiotics, and the WHO warns drug-resistant infections could contribute to more than 39 million deaths over the next 25 years if trends persist. Only 69 countries, or 38%, have nationwide infection prevention programmes, far short of the 90% target for 2030.
key_points: 173 of 183 surveyed countries now have a national action plan on AMR, up from 79 in 2017.
Only 42 countries said their plans were financed and implemented.

stories.headline: I survived a fire that killed my boyfriend - it was started by his brother

stories.headline: ‘Genocide’ is being weaponised by the West’s enemies
stories.claim: Telegraph columnist argues false genocide accusations, notably against Israel, are being weaponised by Russia and the West's enemies.

He points to the International Court of Justice case brought by South Africa and to a Judge Donoghue clarification that the court made no finding of genocide, only that Palestinian rights could plausibly fall under the 1948 Convention. He also cites Ukraine's former foreign minister Dmytro Kuleba on Putin's use of genocide claims to justify the 2022 invasion. This is a polemical opinion piece rather than reporting, and the claims are contested.

stories.headline: India's wholesale inflation accelerates to 12.29% in October on fuel price surge
stories.claim: India's wholesale inflation rose to 12.29% in October, driven by a surge in fuel and power prices.
stories.summary: India's wholesale price inflation accelerated to 12.29% year-on-year in October, up from 11.39% in September and above the 12.1% Reuters poll forecast. The jump was driven by fuel and power, which rose 32.84% after 25.85% in September, while crude petroleum and natural gas prices surged 70.8%. Retail inflation also climbed to 6.09%, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's 6% tolerance limit for the first time in two years, which has raised bets on a rate hike. Economists expect some cooling in November as global energy prices dipped and oil eased toward $95 a barrel. Wholesale food prices rose 8.58%. The data points to continued pressure on the central bank from energy costs.

stories.headline: Plastic Bottles Travel Up To 120 Miles Upriver Around U.S, Study Finds
stories.claim: A GPS-tracking study finds half of plastic bottles entering North American waters may travel up to 120 miles upriver.
stories.summary: A new study has found that half of the plastic bottles entering Great Lakes and ocean waters in North America may have travelled from as far as 120 miles upstream. Researchers led by Ocean Conservancy and the University of New Hampshire tracked more than 300 GPS-equipped bottles for a year across 30 river stretches in seven coastal watersheds. River flow was the main driver of movement, while forest cover and urbanisation also mattered. Bottles in Southern California sometimes travelled over 50 kilometres in 90 days, whereas some in forested Boston moved only a few hundred metres. The findings suggest that storms can carry trash further downstream.

Nagahama and former deputy governor Masazumi Wakatabe, both picked by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, are seen by markets as backers of looser fiscal and monetary policy.

stories.headline: ECB VP says AI, debt have become prominent stability risks
stories.claim: ECB Vice President Boris Vujcic warned AI-related risks and euro zone sovereign debt have become prominent financial stability threats.
stories.summary: European Central Bank Vice President Boris Vujcic said on Monday that artificial intelligence and sovereign debt now stand out "very prominently" among the euro zone's financial stability risks. In a Frankfurt speech he argued that AI has moved from being an equity valuation worry to a systemic risk affecting debt and equity markets, cyber security and operations. He pointed to the roughly $5.5 trillion financing need of major US technology firms through 2030, which is pushing up debt and equity issuance and creating opaque off-balance-sheet structures. He also warned that AI-powered cyberattacks are growing more capable, and that a sharp rise in long-term borrowing costs could strain fiscal positions in highly indebted euro countries. The remarks add to the ECB's long-standing concerns about stretched AI valuations and debt sustainability.
key_points: Vujcic said AI and sovereign debt stand out 'very prominently' among euro zone financial stability risks, speaking in Frankfurt on Monday.

Some regions saw increases, including 31.4 percent in Colombia, 25.4 percent in India and 70.7 percent in Honduras. The work uses satellite data and treats the pandemic as a natural experiment.

stories.headline: US manufacturing is back and better
stories.claim: A Kearney report finds Trump's tariffs did not significantly boost US reshoring, though imports shifted away from China.
stories.summary: A new Kearney report casts doubt on the White House claim that Trump's tariffs have delivered the largest reshoring wave in American history. Kearney finds the tariffs did not drive significant near-term reshoring or reduce total US import dependence. Imports from China fell by $135 billion in 2025 relative to 2024, about 10 percent, while imports from 13 other Asian countries rose by a combined $193 billion, suggesting production is moving to Vietnam, Malaysia and India rather than the US. stories.headline: Vulcan rocket fails on first Amazon Leo launch, losing 40 satellites and likely grounding rocket
stories.claim: ULA's Vulcan rocket failed on Sunday, losing 40 Amazon Leo satellites, and is expected to be grounded indefinitely.
stories.summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket failed about ten minutes into its Sunday launch from Cape Canaveral, losing 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. It was the first total mission failure for ULA since it was formed in 2006. The rocket was a custom six-booster Vulcan with a Centaur V upper stage built for low Earth orbit, and the boosters and fairing separated normally before the anomaly. Sources told Ars Technica the fault lay in the booster stage, which kept burning for at least 30 seconds past its planned shutdown, and the Centaur upper stage then tried to correct the spin. ULA says it will investigate the cause and provide updates, and the rocket is expected to be grounded for an indefinite period. The setback hits Amazon's plans to challenge SpaceX's Starlink with its Leo network, which has 396 satellites in orbit against a planned 3,292. Amazon has 37 more Vulcan launches booked, and the grounding threatens US Space Force launches and NASA's Artemis programme. The next mission, LV-02, was due within weeks and is probably on hold.

stories.headline: Apple launches Health AI Usage Study with OpenEvidence, seeking 200,000 US participants
stories.claim: Apple has launched a Health AI Usage Study with OpenEvidence, seeking up to 200,000 US adults to rate AI health answers.
stories.summary: Apple has launched the Apple Health AI Usage Study, a research programme run with the clinical AI platform OpenEvidence that asks members of the public to test AI health answers. Enrolment opened on Sunday through a new iOS app, and Apple is recruiting up to 200,000 participants. Those eligible must live in the US, be 21 or older and own an iPhone 15 Pro or later running iOS 26 or newer. Participants ask text-based health questions and rate the answers for accuracy, detail and relevance; the answers draw on peer-reviewed sources such as the New England Journal of Medicine and JAMA. The app does not use Siri or Apple Intelligence. Users may optionally share HealthKit data such as activity, sleep and lab results, and Apple says participant data stays confidential and will not be used to train AI models, though it may inform feature development. Participation can last up to 12 months, with surveys included. The study comes as about one in three US adults already use AI chatbots for health information, and it aims to shape how health AI tools are designed.

stories.summary: A $1,982 pair of Clarks Wallabees is the headline price of a very limited collaboration that took nearly three years to make. Kith founder Ronnie Fieg commissioned Japanese artisans Proleta Re Art to mark Kith's 15th anniversary, producing a small capsule under his 8th St by Ronnie Fieg sub-label. Each of the four colourways uses vintage deconstructed denim, antique indigo bandanas and nearly century-old fabric, joined by boro patchwork and hand stitching in Tokyo. The shoes are tied to Kith's flagship cities, Tokyo and Osaka, Manhattan, Paris and London, and will be sold only through those stores. The release goes live on Monday at 11 a.m. ET via the Kith app, kith.com and select stores, in what are described as extremely limited quantities.

Each pair is handmade in Proleta Re Art's Tokyo atelier using boro patchwork and sashiko-style stitching.

stories.headline: School politics class: Democrats need to use the power of the purse
stories.claim: Rep. Greg Stanton says Democrats should use budget leverage to counter Trump's Russia sanctions waiver and Iran war.
stories.summary: Democratic Congressman Greg Stanton of Arizona has said his party should use its budget power to push the Trump administration on Russia policy. Speaking on NewsNation, he argued that Congress passed sanctions on Russia, but Trump waived energy sanctions in October and has not implemented them. The next budget deadline is 11 December, and Senators Sanders, Bennet, Van Hollen and Duckworth have said they will oppose any stopgap spending bill that does not restrict funding for the Iran war. Trump defended the waiver on Truth Social, saying sanctions would have halted hostage talks over the release of a detained US citizen, Stephen Hubbard. The remarks mark a push by Democrats to use spending bills as leverage now that they hold the House majority. Whether they can make it stick depends on the December negotiations.
key_points: Rep. Greg Stanton (D-Ariz.) said on Sunday that Democrats should use the power of the purse to shift US policy towards Ukraine.
Trump issued an executive order in October waiving energy sanctions on Russia and its top energy buyers.

stories.headline: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
stories.claim: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi raises $24M seed round to build AI-enabled image sensors aimed at global markets.
stories.summary: An Indian semiconductor startup, Bharat Semi, has raised $24 million in an all-equity seed round to develop programmable AI image sensors. The New Delhi-based company, which is pre-revenue, says it has design wins with US defence technology firm General Atomics and India's Kaynes Semicon. Its sensors combine image capture, processing and AI on one chip, which its co-founder says could cut system costs by at least 70%. Initial commercial production is targeted for 2027, with a second generation expected at prototype stage by mid-2027. The round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures. The story underlines India's push to become a chip design and manufacturing alternative to China, though the company remains fabless and its fabrication plan is still in development.

stories.headline: Key Takeaways From Luxury’s Q3 Earnings
stories.claim: Luxury groups' Q3 2026 sales slowed sharply as China weakened, with Kering down 17% on its results.
stories.summary: Luxury's third-quarter 2026 results disappointed as China's slowdown deepened, with the sector's average organic sales growth falling to 4% from 7.8% in the second quarter, according to Goldman Sachs. Kering shares plunged 17% after organic growth slowed to 1% from 2%, with Gucci down 6%. Kering and LVMH are each down 37% year to date, and Hermès is off 36%. Richemont's jewellery maisons such as Cartier slowed to 14% growth from 24%, while Ralph Lauren's Asia revenue rose 28%. Analysts see Q3 as the likely trough, but expect China to stay tough for the next two or three quarters, which keeps investors cautious.

stories.headline: Fashion Sourcing Is Big Business. Luxury Is Catching On.
stories.claim: Italian court placed Loro Piana under 12-month judicial administration over worker exploitation in its supply chain.
stories.summary: Loro Piana, the Italian cashmere house owned by LVMH, was placed under a 12-month court administration last week over alleged worker exploitation in its supply chain. Milanese prosecutors found that a Chinese-run subcontractor passed cashmere jacket work to illegal workshops on the outskirts of Milan, where ten workers, five of them undocumented, were reportedly forced to work up to 90 hours a week for as little as €4 an hour. The brand is not under criminal investigation, and the order can be lifted if it meets legal requirements before the deadline. Loro Piana says it cut ties with the supplier within 24 hours of being alerted on 20 May. It is the fifth Italian fashion house placed under court monitoring since 2023, after Armani and Dior, which were both released early in February. The case deepens scrutiny of the Made in Italy label.

stories.headline: Uber drivers’ licence data stolen in Fireworks AI hack
stories.claim: Hackers stole Uber driver licence data via AI vendor Fireworks AI; at least 7,870 people so far in three states.
stories.summary: Uber is warning drivers that hackers stole their personal details and driver's licence information through Fireworks AI, a vendor that sells developers access to open AI models. Uber's state filings this week list 2,567 people in Massachusetts, 3,430 in South Carolina and 1,873 in Rhode Island, a total of 7,870, with California and Illinois also notified without counts, so the figure is likely to rise. Fireworks, valued at $17.5bn in July, told Uber in October that attackers had stolen internal credentials, which were then used to reach Uber's data. It is Uber's second known breach this year after an Uber Freight incident in August. No group has claimed the theft, and it is unclear why driver licence data sat with an AI provider.

stories.headline: UK extends Palantir NHS data contract to 2029, opens tender favouring British firms
stories.claim: The UK government will extend Palantir's NHS Federated Data Platform contract to March 2029 and open a tender for British firms to replace it.
stories.summary: The UK government will not trigger the break clause on Palantir's NHS Federated Data Platform contract, instead extending it by two years to March 2029, according to health minister James Frith, who told MPs the software firm's role would end then. The decision gives time to select British companies to replace Palantir, and the Department of Health and Social Care plans a new procurement process in which UK alternatives can bid. The Financial Times reported that several British firms are preparing bids, including Drystone Health AI Collaboration, a consortium of more than 20 companies led by Shane Tickell of Temple Black, and London-based Quantexa, which is seen as a frontrunner if a British firm is favoured. Oracle Health may also bid. The published contract notice lists a value of £182.2 million, with a forecast of up to £330 million that is not committed. Labour and Liberal Democrat MPs and campaigners such as Amnesty International criticised the extension, having urged ministers to trigger the break clause. The Guardian found 29 trusts used the platform rarely or never, and NHS England removed a claim that 137 trusts used it.

stories.headline: ‘Prove you are not a robot’: how the Captcha scam captures your computer
stories.claim: The ClickFix scam tricks users into pasting malicious code via fake Captcha checks, and is now one of the most common ways to infect computers.
stories.summary: A scam known as ClickFix is becoming one of the most common ways criminals infect people's computers with malware, according to Malwarebytes researcher Chris Fistonich. Instead of the familiar image or letter Captcha, victims are told to press keys such as Windows Key plus R, then Ctrl plus V and Enter. This copies malicious code into the clipboard and runs it on the device. The scam is especially effective during the Christmas shopping season, when people visit unfamiliar small-business websites. Fistonich says people are not prepared for it because they trust Captchas and security software. Advice includes pausing before following any on-screen instructions, using security software that blocks malicious sites, and, if compromised, contacting the bank and changing passwords.
key_points: ClickFix fakes a Captcha and asks users to press keys that paste and run malicious code on their computer.
Malwarebytes researcher Chris Fistonich calls it the most popular way to get malware onto a computer today.

stories.headline: How Dual-Class Stock Entrenches Founder Control at Anthropic, SpaceX, Google
stories.claim: Anthropic's IPO filing uses a five-class share structure giving co-founders 50.1% of votes, part of a wider trend of dual-class control.
stories.summary: Anthropic's S-1 filing, made on 26 October 2026, sets out one of the most founder-friendly share structures yet seen in a major listing. A single Class F share, issued to a Founder LLC owned by its seven co-founders, will carry 50.1% of voting power despite having no economic rights, leaving all Class A public holders with just 49.9% of the vote. A Long-Term Benefit Trust holding Class T stock will elect most of the board, and employees receive Class E shares with limited voting rights. The structure follows Alphabet, Meta and Snap, where founders also hold outsized control. The piece argues that as AI capital needs grow, public investors are increasingly buying economics without meaningful influence over the company.
key_points: Anthropic's S-1, filed on 26 October 2026, creates five share classes that split economic rights from voting control.
A single Class F share given to a Founder LLC of seven co-founders will carry 50.1% of total voting power with no economic rights.
The Long-Term Benefit Trust elects and removes a majority of the board through Class T stock, which also carries no economic rights.
A 450-day Class F Transition Period starts if fewer than three continuing founders remain for 90 days, after which the Class F and E stock is redeemed.
Alphabet's founders hold about 52.7% of voting power via Class B stock, and Snap's two co-founders control over 99% of votes.
stories.market_take: Public investors in Anthropic's offering would get economic exposure but little say over governance, a point that may weigh on valuation debates.

stories.headline: This hypercar wants you to ride it like a motorbike
stories.claim: Dutch startup Sanrivatti unveils the ONE, an ultralight single-seat hypercar with a motorbike-style riding position.
stories.summary: A Dutch hypercar maker, Sanrivatti, has revealed the ONE, a single-seat hypercar weighing about 1,100kg dry that puts the driver astride the centre spine, as on a motorbike. The company calls this the Apex Position and claims that in virtual testing at Corner Three of Silverstone it gave 3.2 times more visible racing surface than ten benchmark hypercars and track cars. The car has a carbon-fibre monocoque, a high-revving V10 from Power, and a fighter-jet-inspired canopy and wing. Interior images have not yet been released, and the company says it will share more as the car is revealed. Sanrivatti's founder, Santiago Sánchez Rivero, says the aim was to rethink how a hypercar feels to drive rather than simply add power.

It uses a high-revving V10 from Power and a carbon-fibre monocoque.
The driver sits astride the central spine in what the company calls the Apex Position, similar to a motorbike.

stories.headline: Bali’s Moon Gang Hotel Finds New Life Without Starting From Scratch
stories.claim: Sydney studio YSG turns a water-damaged Ubud villa into a five-suite hotel, Moon Gang, using local makers and reused materials.
stories.summary: Sydney studio YSG has converted a deteriorating vacation residence in Ubud, Bali, into Moon Gang, a five-suite hotel reached by a lane too narrow for cars. The renovation repaired rotten timber, parts of the roof and concrete floors, and crushed old terracotta tiles and breeze blocks were reused for drainage. More than 15 Indonesian makers contributed, including Weedoo Plastics, whose counters and stools are made from recycled bottle tops. The hotel's courtyard pool is enclosed on three sides by suites, and the interiors use lava stone, bamboo, timber and plant-dyed textiles. The reviewer says the narrow access remains a trade-off for guests who need vehicle access.
key_points: Moon Gang in Ubud, Bali, is a five-suite hotel converted from a water-damaged concrete vacation residence.
Sydney studio YSG repaired rotten timber walls, parts of the roof and concrete flooring.
Crushed terracotta tiles and breeze blocks were reused to help with drainage.
More than 15 Indonesian makers contributed, including Weedoo Plastics, which made furniture from recycled bottle tops.
The pool sits in a central courtyard enclosed on three sides by suites and communal spaces.

stories.headline: Reims 502 uses pink palette for "non-referential" commercial building in Mexico
stories.claim: Reims 502 completes Rosadoce, a flexible pink commercial building in Querétaro, Mexico, shortlisted for the 2026 Dezeen Awards.
stories.summary: Mexican studio Reims 502 has completed Rosadoce, an 840-square-metre commercial building in Querétaro that can work as one unit, four spaces or sixteen modules. Its stepped front, described as an inverted stair, lets in daylight while controlling views from the street. The pink lime render, supplied by Nanocal, echoes the rose-coloured quarry stone of the city's historic centre. The seven-metre building uses a semi-basement to add usable area within the height limit. It is on the eight-strong shortlist for the small workplace interior category of the 2026 Dezeen Awards.
key_points: Rosadoce is an 840-square-metre commercial building in Querétaro, north-central Mexico, by Reims 502.
It can function as one unit, four independent commercial spaces or sixteen smaller modules.
The inverted-stair facade lets in light while regulating visibility from the street.

stories.headline: A timber bridge leads the way into this Nova Scotia coastal retreat
stories.claim: RHAD Architects completes Bridge House, a cedar-clad timber holiday retreat on Nova Scotia's South Shore reached by a footbridge.
stories.summary: A holiday home on Nova Scotia's South Shore arrives at its front door by a timber footbridge, a deliberate piece of theatre designed to heighten the sense of arrival. Bridge House, by Dartmouth-based RHAD Architects, is set back on its plot so it cannot be seen from the street, and visitors drive along a path to a parking court before crossing the bridge into the first floor. The entry sequence includes a sheltered outdoor area and a mudroom built for heavy Canadian winter gear. The main living spaces, including kitchen and dining, sit on the piano nobile beneath a double-height hall with a glazed front facing the cove, while bedrooms are upstairs linked by an internal bridge. The cedar-clad volume draws on local boathouses and cabins, and the architects frame it as both rooted in the coast's traditions and contemporary in its response to climate.
key_points: RHAD Architects, based in Dartmouth, designed Bridge House as a holiday retreat on Nova Scotia's South Shore.
The home is set back from the street for privacy, approached by a driveway and a timber footbridge.
The footbridge is described by the architects as a ceremonial threshold between landscape and architecture.
Living spaces sit on the first floor under a double-height glazed hall facing the cove; bedrooms are upstairs.
The cedar-clad form takes cues from local boathouses and cabins and the coast's vernacular architecture.

stories.headline: Tant A Temps Design "restores the visual characteristics of Tang architecture" in Chinese cafe
stories.claim: Tant A Temps Design has fitted out the Laibei 1087 cafe inside a Song-era stele museum in Xi'an, China, with reversible, Tang-inspired interiors.
stories.summary: Inside a building dating to 1087 in Xi'an, China, a new café uses a reversible, Tang-inspired design that avoids touching the historic structure. Laibei 1087 sits in the Beilin Museum, built to house stone steles inscribed with Confucian texts and calligraphy. Interior practice Tant A Temps Design, led by founder Wei Chen, followed a minimum-intervention approach: furniture hangs from beams or stands around columns, and new elements are detachable. The bar counter hides all modern services such as air conditioning, plumbing and electrics. The 220-square-metre project includes a rest area, a retail zone and a stone-rubbing workshop, and the studio presents it as a model for adaptive reuse of heritage buildings.
key_points: Laibei 1087 is a café inside the Beilin Museum in Xi'an, a building originally constructed in 1087.
Tant A Temps Design, led by Wei Chen, designed the interiors using a zero-damage, reversible strategy.

A central bar island conceals all modern utilities, including air conditioning, water and electricity.
The 220-square-metre project includes a rest area, retail zone and stone-rubbing workshop.

stories.headline: Foster + Partners creates Area worktable for today's office
stories.claim: Foster + Partners and Kettal have launched Area, a modular worktable system with aluminium columns and concealed power.
stories.summary: Foster + Partners Industrial Design has unveiled Area, a modular worktable system made with Spanish furniture brand Kettal. The range pairs aluminium columns, which hide power cables, with tabletops in shapes from round to rhomboid and materials from timber to terrazzo. Columns come in 90, 160 or 450 millimetre diameters, and the system takes magnetic screen dividers and lighting built into the table. The designers say full-scale models, augmented reality and 3D printing shaped the product, with Kettal involved in development. The launch targets the flexible, collaborative office.

stories.claim: SWA Group's Playbook for the Pyrocene offers landscape design guidance on wildfire risk at community scale, with projects and campus standards.
stories.summary: SWA Group, a global landscape architecture firm, is drawing attention to its 2023 Playbook for the Pyrocene, a guide to reducing wildfire risk at neighbourhood scale. The publication sets out six rules of thumb and 20 strategies, and SWA's climate strategy director Jonah Susskind says they still hold up. Projects cited include a park redesign in Pacific Palisades after January's fire and a Oakland plaza with benches made from felled eucalyptus. SWA is also working with Cal Poly San Luis Obispo on campus-wide fire standards that the California State University system may adopt. The interview is a design and planning feature rather than a market story.

stories.headline: Russian military plane crash in Siberia kills 19
stories.claim: A Russian Antonov An-12 military transport crashed in western Siberia, killing all 19 people on board.
stories.summary: A Russian military Antonov An-12 transport plane crashed in an unpopulated area near Kemerovo in western Siberia, killing all 19 people on board. The Defence Ministry said the aircraft went down near the village of Yagunovo, and preliminary findings point to equipment failure. Crews extinguished a fire at the site, and the Investigative Committee has opened an inquiry into possible breaches of flight safety rules. The An-12 is a Soviet-era turboprop still flying in Russia and other countries. The crash follows a Tu-95 loss in the Amur region in September.
key_points: The An-12 went down near Kemerovo, around 3,000km east of Moscow, with all 19 people killed.
The aircraft normally carries a crew of six, so the number on board was higher than usual.
Preliminary findings point to equipment failure, but investigators have not confirmed a cause.
Russia's Investigative Committee has opened an inquiry into possible flight safety violations.
An earlier Tu-95 crash in September killed six crew members.

stories.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak is spreading and killing at a record pace
stories.claim: Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, is spreading at a record pace with over 11,000 cases and 5,500 deaths.
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than any previous recorded outbreak, with more than 11,000 people infected and over 5,500 dead since it was declared on 15 May. Official data show infections and deaths rising at about double the rate of the first six months of the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic. Insecurity, attacks on health workers, unpaid strikes and slow aid disbursement are hampering the response. Of some $2.9bn pledged, less than half has been paid out. The outbreak is already the second-largest on record globally.

Infections and deaths are rising at double the pace of West Africa's 2014-16 epidemic in its first six months.

stories.headline: Democrats Assail RFK Jr. After U.S. Loses Measles Elimination Status
stories.claim: The US has lost its measles elimination status, prompting Democratic attacks on RFK Jr. and the Trump administration.
stories.summary: The United States has lost its measles elimination status for the first time in more than 25 years, according to the Pan American Health Organization, which also downgraded Mexico and Bolivia. The US has recorded more than 7,700 cases over two years, with over 10 deaths reported. Democrats, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, have blamed Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Trump administration. Kennedy said he recommends the MMR vaccine and blamed pandemic-era disruptions for gaps in childhood immunisation. The CDC said the designation does not itself protect people, and that vaccination does.

The US has recorded more than 7,700 cases of measles in two years, with deaths reported in multiple states.
Mexico and Bolivia were also stripped of the status.

stories.headline: Xi and Putin begin highly anticipated meeting ahead of Trump's arrival in China
stories.claim: Xi and Putin begin bilateral talks in Shenzhen on the APEC sidelines, ahead of a Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral on Thursday.
stories.summary: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin opened their talks in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit, with Putin calling it their 50th personal meeting. The two leaders are expected to discuss energy, including a proposed gas pipeline through Mongolia, and how to handle Donald Trump. Trump, who has been in Manila on a state visit, claimed a large trade deal with the Philippines and securing critical minerals, though few details were given. A first three-way meeting of Xi, Putin and Trump is set for Thursday. Analysts note Beijing's balancing act between backing Moscow and keeping its ties with Europe.
